questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: compute chromatographic resolution
questions.stem: Sample 3401: Two peaks elute at 3.65 and 5.46 min with equal baseline widths of 0.81 min. What is the chromatographic resolution?

options.misconception: inverts the resolution ratio
omits the factor of two in the resolution expression
uses one peak width instead of the sum of both widths

questions.explanation: Resolution is two times the difference in retention times divided by the sum of the baseline peak widths. Equal widths make the denominator twice the width. Omitting the factor of two or inverting the ratio gives a different separation measure.

provenance.author: bank-team-analychem
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: compute theoretical plates from a peak
questions.stem: Sample 3402: A peak has retention time 4.10 min and baseline width 0.33 min. What is log10 of the number of theoretical plates?

options.misconception: omits the square on the time-to-width ratio
inverts the retention-to-width ratio
uses a factor of two instead of squaring in the plate expression

questions.explanation: The number of theoretical plates from a baseline width is sixteen times the square of retention time divided by width. Narrower peaks relative to retention time mean more plates and higher efficiency. Inverting the ratio or dropping the square misstates efficiency.

options.misconception: uses a factor of two instead of squaring in the plate expression
omits the square on the time-to-width ratio
inverts the retention-to-width ratio

questions.explanation: The number of theoretical plates from a baseline width is sixteen times the square of retention time divided by width. Narrower peaks relative to retention time mean more plates and higher efficiency. Inverting the ratio or dropping the square misstates efficiency.

questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: compute chromatographic resolution
questions.stem: Sample 3485: Two peaks elute at 7.57 and 8.72 min with equal baseline widths of 0.94 min. What is the chromatographic resolution?

options.misconception: uses one peak width instead of the sum of both widths
omits the factor of two in the resolution expression
inverts the resolution ratio

questions.explanation: Resolution is two times the difference in retention times divided by the sum of the baseline peak widths. Equal widths make the denominator twice the width. Omitting the factor of two or inverting the ratio gives a different separation measure.
